status: source review clear; production maximum native confirmation owned by root
scope: Read-only independent review of shared canvas export manual-capture repair, lifecycle tests and sequence captured renderer consumption. No new test, browser, media encode or build was run by this reviewer.

producerEvidence.scope: Six new controlled manual-capture cases plus six existing byte/abort export bounds and ten existing lifecycle cases; lifecycle suite also contains WebXR cases. These are controlled Node tests, not native codec evidence.

reviewChecks: The first actual draw occurs before capture, recorder starts before initial requestFrame, and no artificial timestamps or accelerated draw loop replace elapsed performance/RAF time.

captureStream(0) probe is owned immediately; absence of requestFrame stops every probe track and clears ownership before one captureStream(30) fallback. Cancellation is rechecked between probe release and fallback, and after each stream acquisition.
Recorder is created only from the selected live stream. Actual requestFrame failure rejects and cleans up; it does not silently restart recording or publish partial chunks.
A draw-triggered retirement is checked before requesting a frame. Initial-request and later-request exceptions reach the shared fail path; finished guards prevent late RAF/data/stop publication.

Manual requests use at least1000/30ms between actual RAF observations, without catch-up bursts. At the end, draw time remains clamped to exact duration and recording waits for the next eligible actual RAF before final request and stop.
Existing duration+10second watchdog and incremental/final32MiB bounds remain. Cleanup clears RAF/timer/listener/recorder callbacks, stops owned tracks, and discards chunks on failure.

Sequence export captures prepareSequence(documentState) before starting, uses its frozen frameAt/sourceFilm/sourceGlobal/camera, and checks operation ownership inside every draw. No live draft is re-read by the exporter.
limitations: The default-capture low frame count observed in two maximum runs does not establish the full underlying browser cause.
The scratch manual-capture result reported by root is experimental evidence, not a claim that all browsers or automatic fallback paths are fixed.
Requesting initial/final frames is not proof that a codec retained exact endpoints; production native decode/PTS/pixel evidence remains a separate root-owned gate.
At most30Hz is a request cadence ceiling, not a guaranteed encoded30fps rate. Scheduling may produce fewer frames.
Waiting for an eligible final RAF can extend the recording by a scheduling interval; elapsed drawing remains clamped and the original watchdog bounds failure.
Fallback applies when requestFrame is unavailable on an acquired probe track. A thrown captureStream call or actual manual request error fails instead of promising universal compatibility.
